seoTitle: How to Buy a Hostinger Domain with Coupon Discounts
metaDescription: Search, register, and save on a Hostinger domain by applying a coupon code at checkout, including what's already included for free before you add one.
intro: Registering a domain does not have to cost full price. First-year pricing varies a lot by extension, and a valid coupon code applied at checkout can push the total down further. This guide walks through searching for a name on Hostinger, comparing what's available across extensions, and getting through checkout with a coupon applied, plus two details that change what you actually pay: privacy protection is included automatically rather than something you add, and only one coupon code applies per order.
costNote: Browsing and comparing extensions is free. What you pay is the discounted first-year rate shown in search results, plus a small ICANN fee on the extensions that carry one and any applicable tax. Renewal in year two is typically billed at the standard, non-discounted rate, so check that figure in the order summary before committing to a name.

steps.heading: Search for your domain name
steps.body: Hostinger's homepage puts a domain search bar in the center of the page. Type in the name you want and hit Search. You don't need an account to search, only to register whatever you find. The same page advertises a free domain for a year bundled with hosting, useful to know if you're setting up a new site from scratch instead of only registering a domain on its own.

image.caption: Hostinger's homepage search bar, where typing a name kicks off the domain availability check.

steps.heading: Compare extensions and first-year pricing
steps.body: Results come back as a list of available names across different extensions, each with its own discounted first-year rate and a Buy now button. Scroll through the tabs for Popular, Business, Technology, and the rest if your first choice is taken or priced higher than you'd like. A different extension can cost meaningfully less without hurting a brand much, but remember the discount only covers year one; renewal pricing resets higher afterward.

image.caption: Domain search results showing multiple extensions with their first-year discounted prices side by side.

steps.heading: Add the domain to your cart and set the registration length
steps.body: Click Buy now next to your chosen name, or Make it yours on one of the featured options higher up the page, to add it to your cart. Choose a registration period from the dropdown, typically one year up to several. Domain privacy protection, which hides your personal registration details from public WHOIS lookups, is included automatically at no extra cost on extensions that support it. You don't need to add it separately; just confirm it's switched on for extensions where it applies.

steps.heading: Enter a coupon code before paying
steps.body: On the checkout page, look for a "Have a coupon code?" link near the order summary. Paste the code in and click Apply, then confirm the total updates before continuing to payment. Only one code applies per order, so a working coupon still stacks on top of whatever first-year discount is already reflected in the sticker price, but you cannot combine two separate codes.

steps.heading: Review the order summary and choose a payment method
steps.body: The right-hand panel breaks the charge down: domain registration for the first year, a small ICANN fee on the extensions that carry one, privacy protection where it isn't already included free, and tax, all rolled into one total. Checkout supports several payment options beyond a card, including PayPal, Google Pay, and Apple Pay, plus regional options in some countries. Pick whichever is fastest for you.

image.caption: Checkout with the order summary — registration fee, ICANN fee, tax, and total — alongside PayPal, Google Pay, and Apple Pay options.

steps.heading: Submit payment and verify your email
steps.body: Complete the payment. Hostinger sends a confirmation to the email on your account, and verifying that address is typically required by ICANN's WHOIS accuracy rules before a new domain fully activates. Once verified, the domain appears in your Hostinger dashboard under Domains, ready to be pointed at a hosting plan or an external platform such as Shopify or WordPress.

troubleshooting.problem: The coupon field says the code is invalid or expired
troubleshooting.cause: Coupon codes carry expiry dates and are often tied to a specific product; a code meant for hosting plans won't apply to a standalone domain purchase, and the reverse is also true.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the code for typos and case, confirm it's meant for domain purchases, and try again before contacting support.

troubleshooting.problem: The price at checkout looks different from the search result
troubleshooting.cause: The search-result figure is a first-year discounted rate; it doesn't include the ICANN fee, tax, or any add-ons that apply at checkout.
troubleshooting.fix: Treat the order summary total, not the headline search-result price, as the number that counts.

troubleshooting.problem: The domain isn't active after payment goes through
troubleshooting.cause: The confirmation email hasn't been verified yet. ICANN requires this for most new domain registrations.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the inbox, including spam, for the address on your Hostinger account and confirm it.

faq.question: Where do I enter a coupon code when buying a domain?
faq.answer: At checkout, in the "Have a coupon code?" field near the order summary, before you complete payment.

faq.question: Do I need to buy domain privacy protection separately?
faq.answer: No. Hostinger includes it automatically at no extra charge for extensions that support it. You only need to check it's switched on, not add it as a paid extra.

faq.question: Can I use more than one coupon on a single order?
faq.answer: No, only one code applies per order. It still applies on top of whatever first-year discount already shows in the search-result price.

faq.question: What domain extension should I choose?
faq.answer: It depends on your audience: .com is broadly recognized, while a country-specific extension like .in suits a local audience, and a cheaper alternative can work fine if the name matters more than the ending.

faq.question: Do I need to verify my email after registering?
faq.answer: Yes. ICANN requires it for most new domain registrations, and Hostinger won't fully activate the domain until you confirm the address on your account.
